newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh launches hunt for rebels after killings.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh launches hunt for rebels after killings.

text.p: Bangladesh's security forces have launched a massive manhunt after suspected tribal rebels killed a soldier and three policemen in troubled southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, security officials said.
They said security forces fanned out in Bandarban Hill district to search for the rebels, who shot the four in a series of attacks on Saturday.
"All probable exit points leading to Indian territory of Mizoram state have been sealed off," a senior army officer told Reuters on Monday.
Bangladesh has about 10,000 soldiers in the Hill Tracts brodering India and Burma.
Officials said the attacks were an attempt to derail the current peace process seeking an end to the decades-old insurgency in the Hill districts.

Security sources have blamed a hardline group within the Shanti Bahini (peace force) opposing a peace intiative taken by the government and the Parbatya Chittagram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political wing of the Bahini, to end the rebellion.
Officials say the two sides made progress at talks in the capital Dhaka last month. The next meeting will be on March 12.

Tribal insurgents have been fighting a bush war for autonomy for 5,500 sq miles (14,200 sq km) of hill tracts bordering India and Burma. They also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency since 1973.
Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Sunday blamed drug and arms trafficking for the rebel attacks.
Hasina added, however, that she was hopeful of a deal to end the bush war.
Tribals and non-tribals including their leaders protested Saturday's killing by observing strikes and transport shutdowns in Bandarban town.
